>
> O ~ poisson_log(log_mu);
> ^-- here

I don't think this one ever would have parsed.

That's the capital letter O, not the number 0.

It took me a while to realize this is what's going
on because our error message is terrible. It somehow
thinks the letter "O" is a vector. It should be reporting
an unknown variable error here. I may have affected that
behavior in my last parser mod for the RNGs in
generated quantities. We're not going so far as to test
for exact error messages when we test if some models pass
or fail.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] parser error
parts:
Never mind. I couldn't replicate the error message until
I looked further up the declarations to data where
the letter O is declared as a vector:

vector[N] O; // observed cases

...

O ~ poisson_log(log_mu);

I don't think we want to extend our Poisson function
to allow continuous inputs --- it looks nontrivial to
normalize properly. The variable O probably used
to be declared as an integer array.

If you want to pass in doubles as proxies for integers > 2^31,
then you can code up the log Poisson density in Stan using
the lgamma and just feed it doubles. You'll still get the
Poisson pmf values. I'm not sure where lgamma will overflow,
either.

For large values of mu, the normal approximation should also
be very good; in Stan, which uses deviation/scale to parameterize
the normal, that'd be:

Obs ~ normal(mu, sqrt(mu));

- Bob

I fixed the issue since 5 days ago.

There were erroneous integer vector types being
declared in function_signatures.hpp; here's the diff:

-int_vector_types.push_back(VECTOR_T); // Eigen vector
-int_vector_types.push_back(ROW_VECTOR_T); // Eigen row vector
+// FIXME: these next two don't look like int
+// int_vector_types.push_back(VECTOR_T); // Eigen vector
+// int_vector_types.push_back(ROW_VECTOR_T); // Eigen row vector

GitHub's "blame" feature makes finding this kind of
thing really easy.

Bad of me to leave commented out dead code in the
file --- I'll just get rid of the lines.

- Bob
